note: Fixtures are FROZEN: they are never edited to make a failing test pass. Each carries the schemaVersion of the release that introduced its type — the WP-01 corpus is pinned at 1.0 and AldusEvent at 1.1 — and every one of them must stay readable by the current build. That is the proof of ADR-0003's same-major rule, not an assertion of it: if a 1.0 fixture ever stops validating, the rule has been broken. A MAJOR bump revisits the whole corpus deliberately (ADR-0003). `jsonSchemaDetectable: false` marks a defect that only the normative Zod schema catches, because the constraint is a cross-field refinement JSON Schema cannot express (ADR-0002).

valid.description: Only the two required fields: who acted and of what kind.
Every optional traceability field populated (§10 backend and session refs).
The four required fields of a persistable failure (§19.1).
Nested cause chain, redacted details, and a timestamp.
Identity, version, and authority only (§9.1).
Scope map, precedence, source revision, and a verifiable content digest.
Durable content identity with no display or legacy metadata (§6.1).
Includes a title and a pointer to a pre-Aldus identity (§4.3).
A source artifact with no declared inputs and unknown size (§8).
An irreplaceable artifact with lineage inputs and a known size (§8.1).
A freshly created Run with no stage entered and no packs resolved (§6.2).
A Run parked on a human gate, with a snapshotted pack set (§5.1, §9).
A queued attempt that has not started and consumed nothing (§6.3).
A failed retry recording its inputs, outputs, actor, and structured failure.
A stage that has not yet been attempted (§6.3).
Two append-only attempts with strictly ascending ordinals (§6.3).
An approval bound to nothing, with invalidation explicitly declined (§13).
A hash-bound decision that expires if any bound input changes (§13.2).
A pre-execution cost preview, with no actual charge yet (§19.3).
A charged cost traced to its authorising decision and provider request (§13.2, §15).

A provider charged the request and withheld the amount: `billingStatus: unknown` is itself the billing evidence, and a fabricated zero would assert a number where the truth is an uncertainty state (§19.3, #150).
An in-flight operation whose outcome is not yet known, awaiting reconciliation (§17).
A failed operation carrying its remote identity and structured failure.
Only the fields §6.4 requires unconditionally: identity, timing, scope, action, actor, and empty reference lists.
Every optional field populated, including a state transition, an idempotency key, an explicit sequence ordinal, and a redacted error.
Only identity, version, and authority — the fields §9.1 requires unconditionally.
Every optional field populated, including dependencies, declared claims, indexed resources, and §9.3 negative knowledge.

invalid.description: `kind` outside the closed ACTOR_KINDS enum.
`id` empty; actor identity is required for every mutating action (§19.2).
`category` outside the closed ERROR_CATEGORIES enum.
`retryable` omitted; retry classification is required (§19.1).
`authority` outside the closed PACK_AUTHORITIES enum (§9.1).
`contentHash` is not a 64-character lowercase hex digest.
`schemaVersion` missing its MINOR component (ADR-0003).
`showId` omitted; an Episode always belongs to a show (§6.1).
`sha256` is not a hex digest; hashes are load-bearing identity (§8.1).
`sha256` uppercase; two spellings of one digest would compare unequal (§8.1).
`sizeBytes` negative, which indicates a producer defect.
`reconstructability` outside the enum that governs archival (§8.1).
`createdAt` has no UTC offset, so it is not comparable across machines (§5.1, §20).
`status` outside the closed RUN_STATUSES enum (§6.2).
`attempt` is 0; ordinals are 1-based so retry limits stay countable (§19.1).
`actor` omitted; every mutating action records identity (§19.2).
Attempt ordinals descend, meaning a writer overwrote history instead of appending (§6.3). Cross-field refinement — not expressible in JSON Schema.
`status` outside the closed STAGE_STATUSES enum (§6.3).
`decision` outside the four outcomes of §13.
`expiresOnChange` omitted; the invalidation policy must be stated, not inherited (§13.1).
Neither `estimated` nor `actual` present, so the record would under-report spend (§19.3). Cross-field refinement — not expressible in JSON Schema.
`amount` is a number; money is a decimal string because IEEE-754 corrupts totals (§19.3).
`currency` lowercase; ISO-4217 codes are uppercase.
`idempotencyKey` omitted; without it a partial release cannot be safely resumed (§17).
`status` outside the closed RELEASE_STATUSES enum (§17).
`action` absent, so the event records that something changed without recording what (§6.4).
`sequence` is negative, which cannot be a position in an append-only log.
`occurredAt` carries no UTC offset, so the instant is ambiguous across machines.
`authority` outside the closed PACK_AUTHORITIES enum of §9.1.

`version` is a number, as §9.1's own YAML example writes it. The schema requires a string so a manifest and the KnowledgePackRef snapshotted from it agree; parsePackManifest coerces this case before validation, but the raw document is invalid.
`packId` absent, so the pack has no identity to resolve or snapshot against.
`precedence` is fractional; §9.2 precedence is a discrete rung, not a continuum.
